approach.method_basis: The Parent keeps a persistent tree of molecular graph edits rooted at the supplied initial molecules. It selects both initial roots and deeper branches using a count-weighted average of the best completed returns among structurally similar siblings, with exploration accounting separately for completed and pending work. It retains exact mean and maximum return records along every purchased terminal path. A permitted expansion creates a new valid molecular state, then normally makes two additional successful graph transitions before buying a score. Fixed roots, bounded expansion, canonical novelty checks and valid fallbacks keep the process within the announced batch.
approach.novelty: Evaluate the first eligible expanded molecule by changing the rollout horizon from two transitions to zero. This is the single registered parameter adjustment at the no-rollout boundary of the existing tree method. Scoring that frontier may give later descendant decisions more direct feedback while creating fewer unscored occurrences per purchase. There are no completed same-Parent children in the frozen brief; nearby tree experiments changed widening or the return statistic, while this experiment changes only where a normal route reaches the oracle. The concurrent root-selection experiment retains both rollout transitions and answers a separate question.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-5cc901d1a9e3 spends its accepted-feedback tree on broad, mostly singleton creation despite the measured best-return selector. Its complete Search mean is 0.32678476606627965 (SD 0.04159141942323312), +0.015171463365010665 against its mean-selector code Parent n-4e4e248bd6bd, but 0.2802455501448513 below formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de. Its three seed changes against its code Parent have mixed signs, so that component progress does not establish reliable endpoint improvement. All published per-seed summary.json and run.log files were read. The new read-only Parent audit reconstructs 13,051 nonroot occurrences for 4,350 optimizer evaluations, 10,644 with exactly one return and 2,280 with at least two. Across 4,351 ordinary expansions, 8,700 extra successful rollout transitions intervene before terminal admission. There are 4,219 eligible first frontiers at the route boundary, but only 21 first-frontier occurrences are directly scored; ten later participate in actual choices and nine receive descendant feedback across announcements (21 such descendant receipts versus three with same-announcement support). This supports testing the location of the expensive observation. It does not establish that the unbought frontier would have scored better. Completed-only widening n-ea747c09699e already increased repeated-occurrence fraction while reducing earlier-batch-supported terminals and full/late gain; this plan does not repeat that refuted conversion hypothesis. Detailed audit and its explicit per-cell audit/log/trajectory/summary/run sources: policy/scratch/r0053-00-improve-L01/audit-parent-frontier-summary.json. Interpretation evidence: nodes/n-5cc901d1a9e3/analysis.json, nodes/n-ea747c09699e/analysis.json, nodes/n-4e4e248bd6bd/analysis.json, nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/analysis.json and nodes/n-29d770e728a6/analysis.json.

adoptions.applicability: The Parent already creates valid, complete molecular states at ordinary expansion. The frozen no-rollout boundary tests direct oracle feedback at that point under its measured best-return sibling selector; it is the allocated parameter adjustment of this exact Parent.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Treat early playout termination as a separately testable decision from tree selection and backup.

deviations.adopted_setting: Purchase the true molecular oracle score of an eligible ordinary first frontier, with no surrogate heuristic or minimax backup.
deviations.paper_setting: Game-tree early termination evaluates a truncated playout state with a heuristic; implicit minimax is a separate paper mechanism.
deviations.reason: Every admitted graph state is already a complete scoreable molecule and accepted-receipt-only scoring is a hard protocol invariant.

deviations.adopted_setting: Exactly the frozen two-to-zero successful-transition adjustment, without a horizon sweep.
deviations.paper_setting: Game-specific termination horizons and reported game performance.
deviations.reason: Zero is the meaningful boundary removing unscored suffix construction on this Parent; neither the parameter value nor expected molecular gain is borrowed from paper tuning.

adoptions.implementation_change: Set CONFIG.tree_search.rollout_successful_transitions_after_expansion to zero; the existing _rollout returns its start and _normal_route/_terminal_on_route emits the eligible ordinary frontier, retaining all selection and backup code.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen Search Policy review and its recorded query; no new literature search is claimed. The first source supports separating termination from selection/backup. Adopt only that separation with explicit molecular deviations. The second source supplies a contrary condition: rollouts may preserve useful action ordering under assumptions not established here, so shorter routes are not presumed better. Parent receipts and the failed completed-only-widening conversion motivate this single first-frontier test; no source score is campaign evidence.

sources.applicability: Use that separation to test the zero-horizon boundary in the existing graph tree. Our first expanded molecule receives the real protocol oracle score; no heuristic value substitutes for an observation. Do not import minimax, game heuristics, source horizons or source performance.
sources.finding: The paper distinguishes fixed-depth early playout termination from changing selection or backup, and evaluates it as a separate design choice.

sources.applicability: Contrary condition: removing continuation may lose useful look-ahead. This warrants a falsifiable finite-panel test, not an assumption that fewer edits are always better. No theorem transfers to this graph kernel or finite molecular budget.
sources.finding: Under specific smoothness conditions random rollouts can preserve action ordering; more informed rollouts need not improve search.

hypothesis: Remove the mandatory unscored rollout suffix on code Parent n-5cc901d1a9e3 by the one frozen parameter_adjustment rollout_successful_transitions_after_expansion: 2 -> 0. _normal_route still performs ordinary _expand; _rollout returns that same occurrence; the existing _terminal_on_route and canonical/pending/fallback laws decide whether it can be emitted. The actual oracle scores that existing valid frontier rather than a fabricated intermediate value. Directly scored occurrence-local frontier credit can then affect actual later-announcement choices and receive accepted descendant returns. Keep count-weighted best-return exploitation at both root and deeper levels, all-return and maximum backup, N+O widening and every graph-operator law fixed. Loss of rollout-only finishing calls follows solely from the zero horizon. The frozen contribution question is whether the two-transition suffix helps or harms useful first-frontier feedback under this best-return tree; no separate operator or selector contribution is inferred.

finding_summary.headline: First-frontier feedback worked and improved the Parent mean, with uneven gains across seeds.
finding_summary.insights:
The result rules out lack of direct frontier exposure as an unavoidable property of this tree controller: real frontier scores were available to later decisions, and the removal improved both endpoint mean and the registered gain rates. It supports a conditional negative contribution of the mandatory suffix on this panel. It does not show that the frontier feedback itself caused the improvement: the same removal also eliminates rollout-only finishing opportunities and changes subsequent random draws. Gain mass restates endpoint progress rather than independently corroborating it.

Useful search remains concentrated. By stop, 2,991 of 4,350 scored frontiers had no later decision use, and 2,822 of 4,488 nonroot occurrences had only one return. Fragment-excluded within-batch similarity rose from 0.250 to 0.333 while the sum of session-unique typed scaffolds fell from 2,722 to 1,946. The molecular assessment describes narrower size extremes but repeated inherited aromatic and heteroatom frameworks, with reactive linkages still present among high scorers. A strong polyaryl/amine family in one docking seed accounts for 57.9% of positive task-seed endpoint differences, whereas another docking seed loses 0.379209; the late-rate advantage is correspondingly fragile as a descriptive panel result. A graph proposal scheme that rearranges ring topology and linkers while retaining useful functional-group relationships could address this structural concentration; another rollout-horizon value does not supply that capability. Whether such a generator improves search, whether the suffix effect repeats, and how much of the gain is mediated by frontier feedback remain open. The literature-derived separation of termination from selection operated as registered, but its game heuristics and performance claims were not transferred, and this experiment does not settle the wider tree-search approach.
finding_summary.results: All 15 Search sessions completed. Every eligible first frontier was scored: 4,350 versus 21 in the Parent, with no rollout transition or unexplained bypass. New nonroot occurrences per paid evaluation fell from 3.0002 to 1.0317. Of those scored frontiers, 1,359 later received descendant feedback, versus nine in the Parent; 3,191 purchased descendants had an earlier-scored frontier ancestor and an actual later decision on that route. The 571 descendants with same-batch frontier support were counted separately. Full incumbent gain per evaluation rose 18.0%, from 0.00040791 to 0.00048141; late gain rose 2.36%, from 0.00049374 to 0.00050541. Mean final Top1 increased from 0.326785 to 0.348101, a paired gain of 0.021316 that passes the registered 0.002 target. The three seed changes were -0.071791, +0.119137 and +0.016603. The formal Anchor still scored 0.607030, leaving a gap of 0.258929. Thus the registered activation and useful-conversion prediction passed on this complete panel, while the separate Anchor performance goal did not.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic derivatives with narrower size tails, but persistent reactive bonds and uneven access to useful functional-group arrangements.
molecular.overall_character: For n-85acb9fe7124, the frozen digest and all listed Child and published code-Parent n-5cc901d1a9e3 Search trajectories were read. Each task has 900 accepted records across seeds 0, 1 and 2, including 870 optimizer proposals. Every listed path exists; no task trajectory or Parent pairing is missing. context.comparison marks Child evaluation complete and Parent pairing complete. These are conditional descriptions of this Search panel, not evidence of mechanism activation or component contribution. No separate Anchor chemistry comparison was made. The output is mostly recognizable, medium-sized organic ring chemistry: substituted indoles and carboxamides, diaryl pyrazolines with thiocarbonyl groups, fused nitrogenous diones, oxygen-rich acetals, and aryl-linked saturated amines. Small acyclic fragments and much larger recombined structures remain. In task order, digest ring-closure rates are 0.8793, 0.8253, 0.8299, 0.823 and 0.823; aromatic-token presence rates are 0.8126, 0.6805, 0.6782, 0.6943 and 0.6356. These are molecule-level SMILES-text indicators, not aromatic atom fractions or ring counts. Formal-charge and stereocentre-token rates are zero throughout; this does not mean that protonatable groups or potential stereocentres are absent. In-memory RDKit reading of the full accepted optimizer trajectories finds fewer molecules with at most five heavy atoms and fewer with more than fifty heavy atoms in every Child task than in the paired Parent task, but also fewer distinct nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds in every task. Thus the Child samples a more concentrated structural repertoire with reduced size extremes, not a demonstrated expansion of useful chemistry. It retains plausible amides, ethers and heterocycles alongside peroxides, O-halogen and N-halogen bonds, alkyl bromides, N-N linkages, unusual ring contractions and stereochemically unspecified saturated centres. Sanitizable graphs alone do not establish stable compounds, practical synthesis or drug properties. Scores in the prose are rounded readings of actual receipts; score-gradient statements describe observed associations and do not infer an unseen target structure. Digest final_molecules are late proposals from the last listed seed, not the final incumbent or a pooled panel endpoint.

per_task.generated_character: The better proposals are medium-sized, strongly aromatic molecules built around substituted indoles, diaryl pyrazolines or a linked phenyl/pyridyl system. They combine methoxy/phenol groups, amide or thioamide functionality and, in some cases, thioesters or hydrazine-like nitrogens. The highest observed proposal, CC(Br)(NNc1ccc(F)cc1O)c1cccc(-c2ccncc2)c1, is a brominated, branched aryl hydrazine derivative, not a clean conventional lead. The indole carboxamide COc1c(C)c(C)cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc12 is more conventionally makeable. The full output also contains tiny halogen/oxygen fragments and large linked aromatic assemblies. Parent endpoints instead include a fused lactam, a nitrile-bearing partially saturated ring system, and an allene/thione-containing ring system; both generations mix ordinary heterocycles with questionable edits.
liabilities: The highest proposal contains an alkyl bromide next to an N-N substituent; high score does not establish its stability or synthetic tractability.
Thioester/thioamide combinations, O-halogen fragments and unspecified stereogenic centres complicate an otherwise recognizable medicinal-chemistry scaffold set.
missing_features: Many low-scoring proposals lack the combined aromatic scaffold and appropriately connected nitrogen/oxygen functionality present in this task's better examples.

The observed successful neighbourhood lacks consistent exploration of chemically stable alternatives to the brominated hydrazine and sulfur-rich appendages. The trajectories do not identify a particular unseen heterocycle as required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The brominated aryl hydrazine scores 0.423820; the indole carboxamide scores 0.382775 and the thioester/thioamide indole CSC(=O)CNC(=S)c1cc2[nH]c(-c3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(O)c1C scores 0.395761. Small fragments such as FOF and OBr score zero, as does a much larger concatenated pyrazoline structure. The association is with retaining an organized aromatic/heteroatom framework at intermediate size, not with adding atoms or aromatic rings indiscriminately. The best supplied initial score is 0.305105. Child seed endpoints are 0.395761, 0.423820 and 0.374873 versus Parent 0.402829, 0.398759 and 0.404656, so the change in chemistry is not a uniform improvement across seeds. Last proposals in all Child seeds are well below their incumbents.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring output is densely aromatic and often fairly large: indole carboxamides decorated with methoxy, fluorine, sulfonamide or thiocarbamate groups, together with extended aryl chromenone/nitrile structures. The best molecule, CCN(C(C)Oc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(F)c1OC)S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(CC(C)C)c1, combines an indole carboxamide with an aryl sulfonamide through an N/O-substituted carbon. Conventional amide and aryl-ether chemistry coexists with contracted ring systems and peroxide/O-bromine derivatives. Parent high scorers similarly retained decorated aromatic frameworks, including an indole amide, a fused ester-rich aryl system and an aryl-ether/amide heterocycle. Ring content is substantial in both generations.
liabilities: Some highly scored structures contain contracted fused rings or peroxide and O-Br bonds, which make their practical synthesis and stability questionable.
The best structure is bulky and heavily substituted, with an N/O-substituted carbon; no synthesis route or stability evidence accompanies it.
missing_features: What is missing from many lower proposals is coherent retention and repositioning of the decorated aromatic/amide environment seen in the upper band, rather than ring chemistry itself.

The upper band does not provide evidence that unusual ring contraction, peroxide addition or indiscriminate aromatic growth is necessary; stable scaffold alternatives with the same functional-group relationships are incompletely represented among these examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best Child receipt is 0.561997; the supplied fused dione already scores 0.548381. A contracted-ring derivative scores 0.561871 and a peroxide/O-bromine indole derivative scores 0.558511. Water, O, scores 0.5, while the larger aryl sulfonyl/carbonyl structure CC=C(C=CCC(C)NC(=O)S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1)c1cc(F)cc(OC)c1 scores 0.266640. Thus the broad baseline and narrow upper band cannot be read as a gradient of chemical quality or molecular size. The better observed examples preserve particular decorated aromatic arrangements, but this panel does not isolate which motif earns the score. Child endpoints 0.561997, 0.556022 and 0.561542 are below the respective Parent endpoints 0.569340, 0.570090 and 0.577577; late Child proposals still include water and large hybrids.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring seed-1 family consists of bulky halogenated polyaryl molecules with an N-alkyl pyrrolidine, amide or aminomethyl connection, and additional amine-bearing side chains. The best molecule contains an aminal-like branched diamine region and an alkyl bromide. There are also less elaborated amidine/sulfone structures and phenolic N-methyl unsaturated five-membered amines in other seeds. Low-scoring examples include much smaller fluoroanilides, thiocarbonyl-containing amides and N-chlorinated pyrazolines. The output therefore does contain potentially basic ring nitrogens; their complete absence would be an incorrect diagnosis.
liabilities: The strongest family is bulky and halogen-rich; alkyl bromides and aminal-like centres create chemical liabilities unrelated to the measured score.

Potential stereocentres and protonatable groups are present, but the emitted strings specify neither stereochemistry nor formal charge. A neutral SMILES does not establish the state relevant to the assay.
missing_features: Many lower-scoring molecules fail to combine the aromatic framework and non-acylated amine centre found together in the stronger examples; neither aromaticity alone nor nitrogen count alone suffices in the observed panel.

Stable, less elaborated variants of the same aryl-to-amine arrangements are not consistently represented among the best proposals across seeds. No particular ring identity or target-specific pharmacophore is established by this comparison.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The polyaryl pyrrolidine/amine proposal CCCN(C(N)CC)C(NC(=O)C1CCCN1CC(C)Br)c1ccc(-c2cc(-c3ccc(F)cn3)cc(F)c2Cl)cc1 scores 0.682994. A related bromide-free polyaryl pyrrolidine amide scores 0.603442, showing that the high-scoring family is not confined to an alkyl bromide. The simple fluoroanilide COCC(=O)Nc1ccc(F)cc1 scores 0.0000627731. The visible gradient associates the stronger seed-1 family with both aromatic surface and accessible amine functionality, without establishing a binding pose or a required protonation state. Seed-0 and seed-2 best molecules score only 0.099703 and 0.166620; the latter is CC1=CN(C)C(c2ccc(O)cc2)C1. Child versus Parent endpoints are 0.099703 versus 0.478912, 0.682994 versus 0.227026, and 0.166620 versus 0.098443. The Parent seed-0 best already combined a smaller fluoro/methoxy biaryl with an N-methylpyrrolidine amide, so aromatic/basic-amine chemistry is inherited capability, unevenly recovered here.

per_task.generated_character: The upper group remains close to the supplied fused nitrogenous dione with phenyl and hydroxybenzoate substituents. Its derivatives vary ring nitrogen placement, phenol substitution, ester groups and the saturation or connectivity of the fused core. These are medium-to-large, ring-rich molecules with carbonyl acceptors and aromatic surfaces; some are conventionally plausible, while O-F substitution and unusual ring fusion are not reassuring. Other sampled families include amide/hydroxamate-bearing nitrogen heterocycles, very small acyclic compounds and oversized aryl assemblies.
liabilities: The O-F analogue is a reactive oxygen-halogen structure even though its recorded score exceeds the supplied starting molecule.
Unusual ring fusions, hydroxylamine-containing appendages and brominated thioester tails add synthetic uncertainty; small score differences do not validate these motifs.
missing_features: Much of the low-score output lacks the organized ring/carbonyl/nitrogen environment retained by the stronger fused-dione derivatives.

The current high-score set provides limited chemically conservative alternatives to the initial fused-dione family; successful reorganization beyond that family is not consistently recovered, despite the distinct Parent example.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied fused-dione molecule scores 0.167839 and remains the seed-0 incumbent. The added-ring-nitrogen variant CCOC(=O)c1ccc(O)c(-n2nc3c(c2-c2ccccc2)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n3C)c1 scores 0.174258. The O-F analogue and a rearranged, partially saturated fused-core analogue both score 0.171499. S, OOF and N#CCCN score zero. The visible contrast favours retention of a connected aromatic/carbonyl-rich scaffold over fragmentation, with modest gains from particular local changes; it does not establish why the reactive O-F variant gains. Child endpoints 0.167839, 0.171499 and 0.174258 compare with Parent 0.182574, 0.167839 and 0.167839. The Parent seed-0 improvement used a different polycyclic amide/hydroxamate and quinoline-ether arrangement, showing that the current successful fused-dione neighbourhood is not the only observed route. Late Child samples still include small brominated fragments.

per_task.generated_character: Higher-scoring molecules occupy distinct medium-sized families: diaryl or aryl/pyridyl pyrazolines with nitrogen/oxygen-rich substituents and thiocarbonyl groups, and partially dearomatized, fused or bridged nitrogen rings carrying methoxy groups and a fluoroaryl amide. The seed-0 best, OCNC(=S)C(=S)N1N=C(c2cccnc2)CC1c1ccc(O)cc1, has adjacent thiocarbonyls, a hydroxymethyl-bearing nitrogen and an N-N ring. Another upper example has an O-N-N-C chain. The seed-1 best is an N-hydroxy pyrazoline with an unsaturated alcohol/enol side chain. Thus improved scores coexist with potentially labile nitrogen/oxygen/sulfur arrangements. Large ester-rich aryl hybrids and tiny fragments persist in the lower output.
liabilities: Adjacent thiocarbonyls, O-N-N chains and N-hydroxy unsaturated systems raise stability and synthesis concerns that were not measured by the score.
The fused/bridged products introduce stereogenic and geometric complexity without specifying stereochemistry; carbonyl and heteroatom counts alone do not make these tractable leads.
missing_features: The lower output often lacks the compact, heteroatom-rich but organized ring structures of the better examples, tending instead toward small fragments or large concatenated molecules.

The upper families lack a demonstrated series of chemically stable replacements that preserve their favourable size and heteroatom arrangement while removing unusual N-O/N-N chains, adjacent thiocarbonyls or strained ring connectivity. No specific unseen target motif can be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The adjacent-thiocarbonyl pyrazoline scores 0.342118; ONNCN1N=C(c2ccccc2)CC1c1ccc(O)cc1 scores 0.316416. The fused nitrogen-ring fluoroaryl amide COC1=CC23C=C(N=C(N2)C(=O)Nc2ccc(F)cc23)C(OC)=C1OC scores 0.320324, while a related late variant scores 0.232242. A nearby rearranged ring system at seed 2 evaluation 296 scores only 0.000532795. Large concatenated ester/aryl molecules can score exactly zero and the task-wide digest median is zero. The contrast is consistent with a sensitive balance of overall size, saturation and heteroatom arrangement; it does not show that thiocarbonyls or N-O bonds themselves are required. Child endpoints 0.342118, 0.222148 and 0.320324 exceed the paired Parent receipts 0.292719, 0.097084 and 0.266085. Parent high scorers already included compact nitrogen heterocycles but also an O-Cl chain and a ketene-containing derivative, so stronger Child scores do not establish chemically safer output.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-85acb9fe7124, complete frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, compared descriptively with code Parent n-5cc901d1a9e3. Full trajectories show smaller size extremes than Parent, yet late proposals still include isolated inorganic or tiny organic fragments and very large joined scaffolds. Its stronger receipts more often retain organized aromatic/heteroatom systems; both small fragments and large hybrids occur among low scores. The broad score baseline in one session prevents treating this as a universal size rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve an informative ring and functional-group framework while controlling molecular size.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs size-changing edits that can retain useful functional-group relationships and meaningful connected scaffolds. Let accepted current-session feedback determine which size and degree of elaboration are useful; this evidence does not justify a fixed target size, a new reward term or a universal fragment ban.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-85acb9fe7124 on the same complete Search panel. Upper-scoring examples include a brominated aryl hydrazine, an O-F substituted fused dione, adjacent thiocarbonyls, O-N-N chains, alkyl-bromide-bearing polyaryl amines and peroxide/O-Br derivatives. A bromide-free member of the polyaryl amine family also receives a strong score. Related reactive motifs occur in published Parent output, so this is a persistent output limitation rather than attribution to the current intervention.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can reach high-scoring structures without demonstrating chemically stable alternatives to their reactive linkages.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically conservative ways to change heteroatoms, linkers and saturation while preserving the topology of a promising structure, so stable alternatives can compete using only the session's observed scores. These observations do not identify a causal score benefit for the reactive bond or authorize replacing the objective with a chemical-quality filter.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-85acb9fe7124 versus published code Parent n-5cc901d1a9e3, all matched Search sessions. In-memory reading finds fewer distinct nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds in every Child task. High-score molecules repeatedly use indole amides, pyrazolines, fused nitrogenous diones or polyaryl saturated amines. The strongly scoring polyaryl/amine family is concentrated in one Child seed; basic amines and rings themselves are not absent. Parent examples show additional successful arrangements.
transferable_gaps.gap: Successful functional-group arrangements remain concentrated in a limited set of inherited scaffold neighbourhoods despite many distinct emitted graphs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is controlled rearrangement of ring topology and linker geometry while retaining useful donor, acceptor and potentially ionizable-group relationships. Expand access to alternative arrangements through task-agnostic graph transformations and current-session evidence, without naming a target scaffold or importing molecules from another session. Scaffold counts alone do not prove useful diversity or explain score changes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-85acb9fe7124 frozen molecular digest and full Search trajectories. Stereocentre-token rate is zero in every task even though high and low proposals include substituted saturated rings, branched aminal-like carbons and fused or bridged structures. Formal-charge tokens are also absent while potentially protonatable amines are present. These strings establish unresolved representation, not a demonstrated stereochemical or protonation penalty.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures do not resolve stereochemical alternatives introduced by their saturated and bridged ring edits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: If supported by the existing evaluator contract, a task-agnostic representation would need to retain and distinguish chemically meaningful stereochemical states when edits introduce them. Any score benefit remains unmeasured here; do not infer it from token absence or impose a target-specific charge state.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
